entities.summary: Yeongyang Kim clan was one of the Korean clans. Their Bon-gwan was in Yeongyang County, North Gyeongsang Province. According to the research in 2000, the number of Yeongyang Kim clan was 7462. Their founder was Kim Chung, Bureaucrat in Tang dynasty. He was dispatched to Japan as an embassy, but the ship he rode was wrecked. Then, he was naturalized in Silla. He changed his name to Nam Min because he was given "Nam" from the region's name “Runan ” as a surname from Gyeongdeok of Silla. Seok jung, a Nam Min 's son, was settled in Yeongyang County and began Yeongyang Kim clan using the original clan's name Kim clan.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Yeongyang Kim clan played a significant regional role in Korean history, with a notable presence in North Gyeongsang Province. Their founder, Kim Chung, had a lasting impact on the region through his naturalization and establishment of the clan.
